name: Minnesota

laws.summary: State CIO must set accessibility standards for technology, software and hardware procurement that incorporate Section 508 and WCAG 2.0, with CIO-granted exceptions.
Public records of state and local government (incl. cities, counties, school districts) must be made accessible on request, with a $500-per-violation penalty capped at $15,000.

laws.cite: 28 CFR Part 35, Subpart H (ADA Title II web & mobile rule, 2024; dates extended by IFR 2026-07663)
laws.summary: Federal floor: state and local government web content and mobile apps must conform to WCAG 2.1 AA; the April 2026 IFR moved compliance to 2027-04-26 (pop. 50,000+) and 2028-04-26 (smaller entities and special districts).

policy_docs.title: State of Minnesota Digital Accessibility Standard v4.0 (effective 2024-07-01)
Minnesota Council on Disability — Digital Accessibility

applies_to: Executive branch state agencies (legislative/judicial encouraged); ICT procured, developed or substantially modified; contracted external websites. §363A.42 reaches local governments for records on request.

deadlines.what: MN Standard v4.0 (WCAG 2.1 A/AA) effective for ICT procured, developed or substantially modified from this date
ADA Title II rule: state government and local governments with population 50,000+ must conform web content and mobile apps to WCAG 2.1 AA (extended from 2026-04-24 by DOJ IFR effective 2026-04-20)
ADA Title II rule: local governments under 50,000 and special district governments (extended from 2027-04-26)

requires: Apply standard when creating, modifying or procuring ICT
File an exception (undue burden, best meets, fundamental alteration) and provide reasonable accommodation when not compliant
mobile: implied — standard covers all ICT incl. web applications and software under Section 508 definitions; mobile apps not named.
procurement: Statute ties standards to procurement; contracted websites must comply. No VPAT/ACR mandate verified in the standard text.
enforcement: CIO exceptions process; §363A.42 private penalty for inaccessible public records; ADA Title II complaints.
notes: Statute still names WCAG 2.0; the CIO standard raised it to WCAG 2.1 via v4.0. ICT procured 2010-2024 remains under earlier WCAG 2.0 versions of the standard. Office contact MNITAccessibility@state.mn.us.
